Lord Ganesha (sculptures of Ganesha incorporated in the temple structure)

history.dynasty: Associated by local tradition with the Bushahr royal family
history.period: Traditionally associated with Samvat 1802 (1745 CE) - oral tradition, unverified
history.summary: The Narsingh Temple of Rampur Bushahr is a small ancient stone temple with a wooden enclosure on the town's main road, beside the Sutlej River (inditales.com). It is dedicated to Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu. The stonework is old with worn carvings; the temple base is carved as a lotus flower, niches at eye level hold idols of various deities, and the carved wooden ceiling (snow-damaged, periodically replaced) reflects Nagara-style elements; the structure also incorporates stone sculptures of Ganesha. Local tradition links the shrine to the Bushahr royal family: royal daughters and princesses carried their family deity after marriage, and a queen known as Suketi Rani is said to have brought the Narasimha deity to the royal household. The shrine is traditionally associated with Samvat 1802 (i.e. 1745 CE), but this is oral tradition, not a verified construction date (mysterioushimachal.wordpress.com). Narasimha Jayanti is observed here. Coordinates are approximate Rampur-town coordinates (wikimapia: 31 deg 26'59"N 77 deg 37'47"E), since no POI-level position for the shrine was found.

name: Narsingh Temple
town_description: Rampur Bushahr is a historic town on the Sutlej River in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh - the last capital of the Bushahr princely state and a former trading centre on the old Hindustan-Tibet Road, known for Padam Palace and the annual Lavi Fair.

travel.airport: Shimla Airport (Jubbarhatti), about 130 km from Rampur.
travel.railway: Nearest railhead: Shimla (narrow-gauge), about 130 km away; Kalka (broad gauge) is farther.
travel.road: On NH-5 (the old Hindustan-Tibet Road), about 130 km from Shimla; regular buses and taxis connect Rampur to Shimla and nearby towns.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and October to November; Narasimha Jayanti (Vaishakha month, April-May) is the main festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published online; daytime darshan typical of small-town temples.
